text() statements built from module-level SQL fragments (event_buffer.py:375 _UNREAD_IN_ROOM_SQL, message_store.py:553-561 _ROOMS_PAST_SQL with a constant {types} fragment, erasure_store.py:667 UNREFERENCED_BLOB, retention_store.py:145 _UNREFERENCED_BLOBS); every value is a bound :param (:t, :uris, :room_ids, :tenant_id).

Switch Console is the desktop app that installs and launches agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, ...), a local Switch server and Docker, so spawning processes is what it is for. Arguments come from bundled constants (OPEN_IN_APPS, provider registries) or the user's own choices; provider-process.ts spawns with argv arrays and quotes .cmd shims by hand rather than shell:true. 2 hits are test files. One hardening note recorded separately (open-in-app {{path_raw}}).

console/apps/switch-console-desktop/scripts/postinstall.ts:11,55 is a dev-time install script with constant commands; console/packages/agent-providers/src/cline/cline.integration.test.ts:31 is a test. Neither ships in the runtime path.

The word 'token'/'API key' is in the message, not the value: api_keys.py:137,218 log the key's label and user id, agent/auth.py:296 the key id and type, broker.py:1092,2330 and github_installation.py:240 deliberately log type(error).__name__ rather than the exception, so a token inside an error string cannot reach the log.

Patterns built from developer-registered route paths (control-server.ts:45), local filesystem glob matching (local-fs.ts, ssh-fs.ts), PATH expansion (shellEnv.ts) and template fields in the desktop app; 4 are tests. No remote party supplies the pattern.
4 in user-changes.test.ts and 2 in loadtest/ (agents.py:118, controllers.py:84), all ws:// to a local test stack.

Keys are developer constants: codex/profile.ts:167 and opencode/profile.ts:163 walk setting.tomlPath from CODEX/OPENCODE_PROFILE_SETTINGS ('a value stored under a key Codex does not declare is left out'), switch-console-config-file.ts:21 walks typed ShareableLocationSettingsWriteField paths, and vendor-cli.ts:348 only reads.
shellEnv.ts:85 expands the user's own login-shell PATH entries on their own machine.
room-templates/controller.ts:162 validates a room template the local user imports into their own desktop app; allErrors only lengthens the error list shown to that user.

Mermaid previews (mermaid-diagram-preview.tsx:57, -dialog.tsx:27) render SVG from mermaid.render() with securityLevel:'strict' (mermaid-renderer.ts:30); agent-icon.tsx:48 and mcpIcons.tsx:36 inline bundled provider/MCP icon SVGs (workspace agents' icons from the server go through ); IntegrationRow.tsx:111 is not rendered anywhere. The renderer runs with contextIsolation:true and nodeIntegration:false.

bridges/agent/deeplink.py:135,163,168 format the handoff page with html.escape(..., quote=True) into an href attribute, the scheme and host of the target are fixed constants (switchdash://), and console paths are allowlisted (404 otherwise).

Each reads claims from a token the server itself just received over TLS from Microsoft or WorkOS, never to admit a caller: teams/auth.py:285 the Graph app roles (Graph tokens are not verifiable by their holder, documented with a nosemgrep), workos_sign_in.py:136 and members_service.py:115 the expiry only, with the members service as the verifier.
teams/crypto.py:68-69 is RSA-OAEP with SHA-1, the padding Microsoft Graph uses to wrap the dataKey of encrypted change notifications; switching hashes would make Graph's payloads undecryptable.

teams/auth.py:122 sends the certificate's legacy x5t (SHA-1 thumbprint, usedforsecurity=False) beside x5t#S256 because older Entra endpoints read only x5t; it names the certificate and secures nothing.

A performance rule (len(query.all()) vs count()), not a security finding.
Dockerfile.switch, Dockerfile.gateway (nginx), Dockerfile.setup and the BYOI image declare no USER. Hardening, not a vulnerability: none is reachable without first compromising the service it runs.
Image-size hygiene in the BYOI Dockerfile:26,36, not a security property.
The BYOI (bring-your-own-image) Dockerfile is an SSH target for remote agent hosts; exposing 22 is its purpose.

After you've created a flow log, you can view and retrieve its data in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. It is recommended that VPC Flow Logs be enabled for packet "Rejects" for VPCs.

CVE-2026-111064/111066/123817 (high), 111063/111065/111748/111750 (medium). Reachable in part: bridges/collaboration/ingress.py and teams/adapter.py run aiohttp.web servers for inbound platform webhooks, so the missing initial-request timeout (111064) applies to a public listener (availability). 111066 needs Request.post() (not used), 111748 needs Request.scheme in a security decision, 111750 the pure-Python parser behind a disagreeing proxy; the rest are client-side against platform servers.

CVE-2026-96760 (critical), 114615/114616/116672 (high), 114617/114618/114619/114620 (medium). Switch imports only authlib.integrations.starlette_client for its OIDC sign-in, an authorization-code flow whose ID token comes from the IdP's token endpoint. The advisories cover JWS JSON deserialize_json, OAuth/OIDC server endpoints (client configuration, JWT bearer grant, implicit grant, RFC 9101 request objects), implicit/hybrid nonce handling, and HMAC keys from PEM or empty secrets; none is on that path. Still worth the bump: the version is two minors behind.

CVE-2026-63374 (critical: IDNA 2003 vs 2008 when validating a non-ASCII TLS hostname, needs an on-path attacker and an internationalised domain) and 64847 (process-pool stderr). Outbound hosts are ASCII platform and provider APIs.

GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2 (critical): the bundle still trusts the emSign ECC root whose intermediates were compromised and revoked; exploiting it needs an on-path attacker holding one of those keys. Every outbound HTTPS call from the image trusts this bundle.

CVE-2026-59951 is not reachable (the FastMCP server runs stateless_http=True, bridges/agent/mcp/server.py:177) and 116684 needs the SDK's AuthSettings token_verifier, which Switch does not use. 116685 (cross-origin redirects keep custom headers) and 116686 (outputSchema $ref fetches) are client-side: they apply to connections/adapters/oauth.py's fastmcp Client against the connector MCP servers Switch calls.

records.rule: FastMCP: Post-transform component authorization is skipped on direct calls
records.detail: GHSA-7xgj-8392-5q4r on fastmcp and fastmcp-slim 3.3.1: needs server transforms plus component authorization policies; Switch's FastMCP server uses neither.
CVE-2026-119283/119284: JWE recipient and JWS deserialization DoS. joserfc arrives with authlib; the only token it could parse is the ID token from the IdP's own token endpoint.
CVE-2026-114605: DNS wire-format parsing. switch_core never imports dns and parses no DNS messages.
CVE-2026-114603: TraceState.from_header via TraceContextTextMapPropagator.extract on inbound tracestate. switch_core does not extract trace context from inbound requests.
CVE-2026-102991: path traversal on Windows in template lookup. Mako only renders Alembic's migration template; the server image is Linux.
CVE-2026-104874: reference leak in items-view union/subtraction over attacker-influenced sequences; arrives with aiohttp.

Server side: GHSA-f897-62hf-6gxq and CVE-2026-111768 (request-size DoS) are not reachable without the token, because switch-agent-runtime/src/hosted.ts checks its bearer token before the SDK sees the request; 111767 needs the experimental taskStore and 111771 the SDK's bearer auth, neither used. Client side: 104850 (OAuth credentials not bound to their authorization server) and 111769 (cross-origin redirects keep headers) apply to agent-providers/src/host/vendor-mcp.ts against vendor MCP servers.
Five high, three medium (SSRF, host confusion, XSS via URI parsing). fast-uri arrives with ajv for URI format checks on templates the local user imports; nothing fetches based on its parse.
serveStatic, parseBody, toSSG and hono/jsx advisories. Transitive via the MCP SDK; no console code imports hono or serves static files with it.

Address-classification and parsing advisories; no console code makes an allow/deny decision with it.
GHSA-r4xh-jqrq-34v2: quadratic parse of TOML the console writes and reads itself (agent CLI profiles).

Hand review; no tool rule covers them. Three first-party findings (2 High, 1 Medium), each reported privately through GitHub private vulnerability reporting on 2026-11-12, one report per finding, as SECURITY.md asks. Detail withheld until the maintainers resolve them.

Hand review behind a detect-child-process hit. console/.../main/core/app/service.ts:254-266 runs each 'Open in' command template through exec(); {{path}} is shell-quoted per platform but {{path_raw}} is substituted raw inside double quotes (Alacritty, Athas, Trae, Trae Solo, and Windows 'cmd /K "cd /d ..."' in shared/openInApps.ts), where $(...) still expands on macOS/Linux and & ends the command in cmd. The path comes from the OS folder picker, so it needs a booby-trapped folder name the user chose: hardening, not a vulnerability. Fix: quote it like {{path}} or use execFile with an argv.
